title: Targeted Data Fusion for Region-Specific Survival Effects in the AMP HIV Prevention Trials
abstract: arXiv:2501.18798v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The Antibody Mediated Prevention (AMP) trials opened a new scientific frontier by showing that passively administered monoclonal broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) could prevent HIV-1 acquisition. The trials enrolled 4,611 participants across four epidemiologically distinct regions, with 174 HIV-1 diagnoses observed during follow-up. Regional heterogeneity in treatment efficacy, together with privacy and regulatory limits on central data pooling, calls for methods that borrow strength across regions without sharing individual-level data. To estimate region- and treatment-specific survival curves under distributional heterogeneity, we develop a federated learning approach that combines site-specific estimators via an L1-regularized criterion that downweights data sources not aligned with the target. translated_title: AMP艾滋病预防试验中区域特异性生存效应的靶向数据融合
translated_abstract: 抗体介导预防（AMP）试验通过证明被动给予的单克隆广谱中和抗体能够预防HIV-1感染，开辟了新的科学前沿。该试验在四个流行病学特征各异的地区招募了4,611名参与者，随访期间观察到174例HIV-1确诊病例。治疗效果存在区域异质性，加之隐私和监管对中央数据汇集的限制，因此需要能够在不共享个体层面数据的前提下跨区域借力的方法。为了在分布异质性条件下估计区域特异性和治疗特异性的生存曲线，我们开发了一种联邦学习方法，通过L1正则化准则将各站点的估计量进行组合，该准则能够降低与目标不一致的数据源的权重。我们进一步将该框架扩展到一类更广泛的因果对比，包括生存差异、生存比等。
tldr: 针对AMP艾滋病预防试验，提出了一种基于L1正则化准则的联邦学习方法，在不共享个体数据的情况下融合多区域信息，以估计区域特异性和治疗特异性的生存曲线及因果效应。
en_tdlr: A federated learning approach is developed that combines site-specific estimators via an L1-regularized criterion to estimate region- and treatment-specific survival effects in the AMP HIV prevention trials without sharing individual-level data.
